Signing a Halton or Peel new build? The page you skip may cost you.

caption:
Waterloo Region buyer? Move in 2 years and it may cost you far more than you expect.

The first question to ask before buying: how long will I really stay? When you buy and later sell, there are one-time costs on both sides, like land transfer tax, legal fees and realtor fees. On a short stay, those costs have little time to pay off. If you might move in about two years, talk it through before you sign.

Cambridge first home? Don't leave this unclaimed.

The federal Home Buyers' Amount lets a qualifying first-time buyer claim up to $10,000 on their tax return (line 31270). It is a non-refundable credit: it lowers the tax you owe, and you get no refund from it if you owe none. If you buy with a spouse or partner, it can be split only if both of you qualify, and the total can't exceed the maximum.

Source: Canada Revenue Agency, line 31270 Home Buyers' Amount (page modified Jul 29, 2026; it shows tax year 2025). Confirm the current-year amount. Eligibility rules apply.

Oakville seller says “no issues”? Get it in writing.

In Ontario, sellers are generally not required to complete a Seller Property Information Statement. If you are buying, ask your Realtor® whether the seller provided one. Ask about leaks, repairs and insurance claims through the seller's side, in writing. A statement is not a home inspection, so still hire an inspector and ask your lawyer.

Etobicoke offer accepted? Not sold yet.

An accepted offer with conditions is not a final sale until those conditions are removed. Common buyer conditions, like financing or a home inspection, each come with a deadline in the agreement. Until they are waived, the buyer may be able to walk away under the agreement's terms. Ask your Realtor® for every condition date and put them in your calendar.
